games.title: Sokoban
games.note: First released for NEC's PC-8801; the name means 'warehouse keeper' in Japanese.

games.title: Baba Is You
games.note: Began as a 2017 Nordic Game Jam entry; you push word blocks to rewrite rules like WALL IS STOP.

games.title: Stephen's Sausage Roll
games.note: A famously hard block-pushing game about grilling sausages on both sides without burning them.

games.title: Patrick's Parabox
games.note: A block-pushing puzzle game where boxes contain smaller copies of levels, sometimes even of themselves.

games.title: Lemmings
games.note: Grew from Mike Dailly's tiny animation of little men walking to their doom; DMA Design later made Grand Theft Auto.

games.title: The Incredible Machine
games.note: Build Rube Goldberg contraptions from balls, belts, cats and mice to complete each task.

games.title: Contraption Maker
games.note: A spiritual successor to The Incredible Machine; it entered Steam Early Access in 2013 and reached 1.0 in 2014.

games.title: Tower of Goo
games.note: A four-day prototype for Carnegie Mellon's Experimental Gameplay Project, made for the prompt 'make something with springs'.

games.title: World of Goo
games.note: Made by two former Electronic Arts developers working as a two-person studio in San Francisco.

games.title: Narbacular Drop
games.note: A student game where a princess escapes a dungeon by placing linked portals; Valve hired its team.

games.title: The Talos Principle
games.note: Grew out of puzzle experiments during work on Serious Sam 4; written by Tom Jubert and Jonas Kyratzes.

games.title: Superliminal
games.note: Objects become as big as they look when you let go of them; it began as a 2013 student tech demo.

games.title: Antichamber
games.note: A first-person maze where corridors change behind you and signs offer cryptic advice.

games.title: Viewfinder
games.note: Place a photograph in the world and it becomes solid 3D space you can walk into.

games.title: Monument Valley
games.note: Princess Ida walks impossible, M. C. Escher-style buildings that you rotate and shift.

games.title: Echochrome
games.note: Based on Jun Fujiki's OLE Coordinate System: whatever looks connected from your viewpoint is connected.

games.title: Fez
games.note: A 2D world you rotate in quarter turns to reveal its hidden third dimension.

games.title: Superbrothers: Sword & Sworcery EP
games.note: A pixel-art iPad adventure with music by Jim Guthrie, tied to the phases of the real moon.

games.title: Lara Croft Go
games.note: A turn-based Tomb Raider puzzle game played on a board of nodes, following Hitman Go.

games.title: Tunic
games.note: A small fox explores a Zelda-like world, guided by an in-game manual written in an invented script.

games.title: Florence
games.note: A wordless story of first love, where small puzzles act out moments like conversations.

games.title: Angry Birds
games.note: Soft-launched in Finland on 1 December 2009 and released worldwide ten days later.

games.title: Crush the Castle
games.note: A Flash game where a trebuchet hurls stones to topple castles and the royals inside.

games.title: Peggle
games.note: Hitting the last orange peg plays Beethoven's 'Ode to Joy' in slow motion.

games.title: Peglin
games.note: A goblin fights by dropping orbs through peg boards; it left Early Access in 2024.

games.title: Cut the Rope
games.note: Cut ropes to swing a candy into the mouth of the little green monster Om Nom.

games.title: The Room
games.note: An intricate puzzle box you turn and probe, made by six former Criterion developers as their first original game.

games.title: Pipe Mania
games.note: Lay random pipe pieces ahead of the flowing 'flooz'; Lucasfilm Games released it in America as Pipe Dream.

links.took: Sokoban popularized grid-based block-pushing puzzles.
links.added: The blocks are words: push them to rewrite rules like WALL IS STOP.

links.took: Sokoban popularized grid-based block-pushing puzzles.
links.added: Sausages that roll and must be grilled on both sides without burning.

links.took: Sokoban popularized grid-based block-pushing puzzles.
links.added: Boxes that contain whole levels, which you can push yourself into.
links.extra: Wikipedia says its core ideas came from Sokosoko, a small itch.io game by juner.

links.took: DMA Design, the Dundee studio that made Lemmings.
links.added: A top-down crime sandbox of stolen cars and police chases.

links.took: A spiritual successor from Spotkin, founded by Incredible Machine producer Jeff Tunnell.
links.added: Modern physics, a level editor and sharing contraptions online.

links.took: Kyle Gabler's prototype of building towers from springy goo balls.
links.added: A full story, many kinds of levels and a strange corporate world.

links.took: Linked portals; Valve hired the DigiPen students who made Narbacular Drop.
links.added: Aperture Science test chambers, momentum puzzles and the AI GLaDOS.

links.took: Portal popularized first-person test-chamber puzzles built from boxes and devices.
links.added: Laser connectors, tetromino sigils and a philosophical story about consciousness.

links.took: Stylish, minimal indie art on touchscreens, cited among its visual inspirations.

links.added: A wordless love story told through small touch-screen puzzle moments.

links.took: Crush the Castle popularized flinging projectiles to topple physics-based castles.
links.added: Birds as ammunition, each with a special power, and smirking green pigs.
links.extra: Crush the Castle came out earlier in 2009 as a free Flash game.
